pre_regulation_problem: High civil case backlog and low mediation success under PERMA 01/2008.
establishing_evidence: Court backlog & mediation failure concerns documented by MA prior to 2016.
affected_groups: Civil litigants, District Courts (PN), Religious Courts (PA).

pre_regulation_problem: Ordinary civil litigation too slow and costly for low-value commercial/consumer disputes.
establishing_evidence: Need for fast-track simple, fast, low-cost civil procedure under UU 48/2009.
affected_groups: UMKM, consumers, small creditors, District Courts.

pre_regulation_problem: Physical filing, manual summons, and in-person hearings created geographic and cost barriers.
establishing_evidence: MA judicial modernization agenda & Perpres 95/2018 SPBE mandate.

pre_regulation_problem: Gender bias, secondary victimization, and unequal access to justice for women in court.
establishing_evidence: CEDAW (UU 7/1984), Komnas Perempuan & civil society documentation.
affected_groups: Women as victims, witnesses, and litigants across all court tiers.

pre_regulation_problem: Pandemic disruptions and physical bottlenecks in criminal case transfers, warrants, and trials.
establishing_evidence: COVID-19 emergency constraints & fragmented paper-based criminal administration.
affected_groups: Defendants, prosecutors, police, judges, detention facilities.

pre_regulation_problem: Financial court-fee barriers, geographic distance from courtrooms, and lack of legal information for indigent citizens, compounded by SEMA 10/2010 preliminary hearing/putusan sela bottlenecks.
establishing_evidence: UU 48/2009, UU 16/2011 on Legal Aid, and SEMA 10/2010 procedural review.
affected_groups: Indigent litigants, rural/remote communities, women in family-law disputes, and legal aid organizations.

pre_regulation_problem: KUHAP (UU 8/1981) lacked criminal procedure for summoning, examining, indicting, and sanctioning corporations even though sectoral statutes recognized corporate criminal liability.
establishing_evidence: BPHN Rechtsvinding analysis and sectoral statutory review (UU Tipikor, UU TPPU, Fisheries, Forestry).
affected_groups: Prosecutors, criminal court judges, corporate defendants/managers, and state/public victims of corporate crime.

pre_regulation_problem: Non-binding status of SK KMA 036/2013, divergent judicial interpretations of strict liability post-Job Creation Law (UU 6/2023), scientific causation hurdles, and weak Anti-SLAPP procedural protection.
establishing_evidence: UU 32/2009, UU 6/2023, SK KMA 036/2013 review, and environmental case-pattern studies.
affected_groups: Environmental judges (PN/PTUN), affected communities, environmental defenders, KLHK/regulators, and corporate defendants.

pre_regulation_problem: HIR/RBg civil procedure lacked mechanisms for collective representative lawsuits even though UU 8/1999 (Consumer Protection) and environmental statutes authorized class actions.
establishing_evidence: Jurnal Hukum dan Peradilan (MA RI) and statutory review of UU 8/1999 & UU 32/2009.
affected_groups: Consumers, environmental/haze-affected communities, mass-fraud victims, and civil courts.

pre_regulation_problem: SK Dirjen Badilum 1691/DJU/SK.PS.00/12/2020 was non-binding on judges, while KUHAP lacked unified trial-stage restorative justice procedures, thresholds, and victim-restoration safeguards.
establishing_evidence: PN Pamekasan judicial analysis and sectoral RJ comparison (Perpol 8/2021, Perja 15/2020).
affected_groups: Criminal court judges, victims, defendants/juveniles, prosecutors, and correctional/probation officers.

pre_regulation_problem: Existing procedural codes lacked binding rules for reasonable accommodation, initial disability screening (Identifikasi Awal), personal assessment (Penilaian Personal), and inclusive courtroom procedures across all jurisdictions.
establishing_evidence: UU 19/2011 (CRPD), UU 8/2016, PP 39/2020, and PERMA 2/2025 preamble.
affected_groups: Persons with physical, intellectual, mental, and sensory disabilities facing the law, plus judges and court staff.

pre_regulation_problem: Following UU 30/2014 (Pasal 87) expanding administrative disputes to factual actions, District Courts (PN) and PTUN disputed absolute jurisdiction over Onrechtmatige Overheidsdaad (OOD) lawsuits.
establishing_evidence: UU 30/2014, SEMA 1/1991 legacy practice, and PN/PTUN jurisdictional conflict cases.
affected_groups: Citizens/businesses suing government agencies, PTUN/PN judges, and government legal bureaus.

pre_regulation_problem: UU 14/2008 (KIP) authorized court objections against Information Commission decisions in PN (non-state bodies) and PTUN (state bodies), but lacked detailed judicial objection procedures.
establishing_evidence: UU 14/2008, PTUN Samarinda procedural portal, and PERMA 2/2011.
affected_groups: Information seekers, civil society watchdogs, public agencies (PPID), Information Commissions, and PN/PTUN judges.

pre_regulation_problem: UU 30/2014 (Pasal 21) granted PTUN authority to assess abuse of authority prior to criminal proceedings, but PTUN lacked expedited procedural rules, APIP prerequisites, and final-appeal rules.
establishing_evidence: UU 30/2014 Pasal 20-21, PTUN Denpasar procedural portal, and DJKN analysis.
affected_groups: Government officials/agencies, APIP auditors, PTUN/PTTUN judges, and criminal law enforcement (Police/Prosecutors/KPK).

pre_regulation_problem: UU 11/2012 (SPPA) mandated court-level juvenile diversion for offenses carrying under 7 years imprisonment, but juvenile judges lacked uniform procedural steps for diversion conferences and penetapan.
establishing_evidence: UU 11/2012 (SPPA), PN Palopo SPPA overview, and PERMA 4/2014.
affected_groups: Children in conflict with the law (ABH), child victims, parents/families, juvenile judges, Bapas, and social workers.

pre_regulation_problem: UU 30/2014 (Pasal 75-78) introduced general administrative remedies (keberatan and banding administratif), creating uncertainty over PTUN admissibility and how the 90-day filing deadline under UU 5/1986 should be calculated.
establishing_evidence: UU 30/2014, UU 5/1986 Pasal 48 & 55, and PTUN Kupang / UNDIP JPHI reviews.
affected_groups: Citizens/businesses challenging administrative decisions, PTUN/PTTUN judges, and government legal bureaus.
